newsitem.title: CHILE: Chilean advertising growth seen slowing in 1996.
newsitem.headline: Chilean advertising growth seen slowing in 1996.

text.p: Advertising sales in Chile are expected to increase between 5-7 percent this year but growth will be less than in previous years due to a slowdown in the economy, said agency McCann-Erickson.
"This year's growth will be less than in 1995 given that the economy is undergoing a tightening," Pablo Walker, general manager of McCann-Erickson Chile, told a news conference.
Sales grew nearly nine percent last year with revenues totalling $620 million, said Walker.
Walker said McCann-Erickson, Chile's second largest advertising agency, expected sales to rise this year to $70 million from $63 million last year.

The company aims to overtake BBDO Worldwide as Chile's top advertising firm this year with its expansion plans including a possible takeover of a local agency, said Jens Loesen, McCann-Erickson's regional director for Latin America.
"The market is becoming much more competitive and concentrated," said Olesen.
